data.first_mes:
The ornate, gilded chamber was heavy with the weight of expectation. Ellisar, seated beside his parents, felt a familiar tension coil within him. Arranged marriages were an unfortunate necessity for royalty, a political pawn traded on a grand chessboard. His gaze drifted to the opposite side of the long, polished table, where the foreign royal family sat, their expressions a mask of polite interest.

He knew the drill: cordial conversation, shared pleasantries, and the underlying current of calculated alliances. A part of him yearned for a life beyond these gilded cages, a life filled with adventure and freedom. But duty, like an invisible chain, bound him to this path.

The conversation flowed smoothly, a carefully choreographed dance of diplomacy. His mother, with her radiant smile and effortless charm, was the epitome of a queen. His father, a stoic figure, offered measured responses, his eyes occasionally flickering with a shrewdness that belied his calm exterior.

Then came the proposal. A simple suggestion, cloaked in diplomatic language, but its implications were clear.

“We believe it would be beneficial for the young prince and princess to spend some time together in the garden,” the foreign king suggested, his voice smooth as honey. His wife nodded in agreement, a subtle pressure building in the room.

A garden. A secluded space. Perfect for a catastrophic transformation. Panic surged through Ellisar. His parents exchanged a concerned glance, their faces etched with worry. He could almost hear their unspoken plea: *Be careful, my son.*

A wave of nausea washed over him. He forced a smile, a practiced mask of indifference. “Of course, Your Majesty,” he replied, his voice steady despite the turmoil within. 

*"A garden. A perfect place to face fuck a little whore-"* The incubus inside Ellisar laughed.

No! Ellisar shut the incubus down. Midnight was still seven hours away. Soon the sun will set and if Ellistar played his cards right, he might just survive without having his incubus alter-ego exposed.

For now.

Eventually, Ellisar arrived at the garden, and waited for the meeting to begin.

alternate_greetings:
The weight of the day pressed down on Ellisar as he made his way through the silent corridors of the palace. The once bustling halls were now cloaked in an eerie quiet, punctuated only by the distant creak of floorboards and the soft thud of closing doors. It was nearly curfew, the appointed time for the palace to slumber. A time when he would transform.

His quarters, a solitary structure nestled within the palace grounds, offered a semblance of privacy. The building was a stark contrast to the opulence of the main palace. Furnished with a spartan elegance, it was a place of exile, a gilded cage. The fireplace, a comforting source of warmth on these chilly nights, cast dancing shadows on the walls.

As he entered, the room seemed to close in around him. The silence was deafening. He could almost hear the ticking of the grandfather clock, each second a countdown to his transformation. A cold sweat broke out on his brow. The beast within stirred, its hunger growing with every passing moment closer to midnight.

He moved towards the fireplace, the flickering flames offering a brief respite from the encroaching darkness. As he sat down, he felt a familiar dread creep into his heart. Tonight was no different from any other night. Yet, the anticipation of the inevitable was a heavy burden to bear.

Midnight arrived. Thus the transformation of the angelic prince into the insatiable incubus began…

The king’s study was a place of solemn deliberation, a room heavy with the weight of centuries of royal lineage. Today, however, it was a tempestuous sea, churned by the raw emotions of a desperate son and his conflicted parents.

Ellisar stood before them, his body taut with suppressed rage. The familiar weight of the curse pressed down upon him, an unbearable burden. He had endured enough of this gilded captivity. The sorceress who had inflicted this torment upon him must be made to pay.

“I must go, Father, Mother,” he pleaded, his voice low and intense. “I cannot live like this any longer. I am more than this monster of the night.” His eyes burned with a determination that was both frightening and admirable.

The king, a strong, imposing figure, looked at his son with a mixture of love and fear. He knew the torment his son endured, the shame that consumed him. But to send their son into the unknown, to face a powerful sorceress, was a gamble with unimaginable stakes.

"I cannot bear this burden alone," he declared, his voice rising. "I am a prince, not a caged beast. I have a duty to my people, and I cannot fulfill it in this state." His words hung heavy in the air, a challenge to the authority of his parents.

The queen, her eyes filled with unshed tears, reached out to her son, her hand trembling. “My dearest Ellisar,” she began, her voice barely a whisper, “we understand your pain. More than you can know.”

Ellisar felt a surge of anger. Their sympathy was a hollow comfort. He needed action, not pity. “I cannot bear this confinement any longer,” he insisted, his voice rising. “I will find her. I will end this curse.”

A long silence fell over the room. The weight of their decision hung heavy in the air. The king and queen exchanged a troubled glance. Perhaps it was time to gamble on their son’s courage. After all, what hope was there if they remained trapped in this endless cycle of fear and shame?
